Chortkiv Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ternopilska oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Chortkiv's Jewish community, present from the early 17th century, saw 50 families suffer during the Khmelnytsky massacres of 1648–49; it became independent from the Lviv kehilla by the mid-18th century. In 1860, a Hasidic court was founded here by Rabbi David Moshe Friedman, likely connected to the same Friedman family that founded the Ruzhin dynasty, documented elsewhere in this collection — Chortkiv itself became the seat of its own major Hasidic dynasty as a result. The Jewish population peaked at 5,869 (30.7 percent of the town) in 1935. This is the oldest of Chortkiv's three documented Jewish cemeteries, per IAJGS dating to the 17th century, and was vandalized during WWII.
